stops.stop: Fishers Hill, Woking, the last fourteen months
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Arthur Balfour'): immobilised by phlebitis from early 1929, living at his brother Gerald's house at Hook Heath, Woking; visited by Weizmann shortly before the end; died 19 March 1930, aged 81, of circulatory complications, unmarried and childless, having declined a public funeral. The research pool's two lenses gave different coordinates for the house, 51.3128, -0.5928 and 51.3193, -0.5883, about 700 m apart; the first is used here and the divergence recorded. Retrospect: 1848-1886 was published in 1930.
notes: hard triggers (disputed) discounted: the day is explicitly attested and their clause names no date, year, month or number (it concerns the pin, the house or the sources)
soft triggers (year range, year named with preposition) judged to concern the pin, the sources or the surrounding narrative, not the date, because the text cites the day

stops.stop: Whittingehame, the burial ground and what outlives him
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Arthur Balfour'): buried 22 March 1930 beside members of his family at Whittingehame in a Church of Scotland service. The afterlife detail is attested as follows: the statue in the Members' Lobby was unveiled in 1962 and attacked by two Palestine Action activists in 2024; the de Laszlo portrait at Trinity was sprayed and slashed in March 2024 and restored, at a cost reported as roughly 24,000 pounds in an account not confirmed by the college itself; the Israeli commemorative stamp for the fiftieth anniversary was issued in 1967. The quotation is attributed to The Observer in January 1927, the day given variously as the 20th (Wikiquote) and the 30th (Oxford Dictionary of Quotations); the 30th was a Sunday and the paper is a Sunday paper. Tagged [R]; no reproduction of the newspaper was reachable.
stops.sun_caveat: year precision: the Sun could be in any sign; the reading above is for the stated (defaulted or conventional) day and should not be trusted
